A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIGNETTE study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 and Appendix A.3 report original evaluations of three VLMs across factuality, perception, stereotyping and decision-making.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds model comparisons, human validation, prompt robustness tests, alternative image generation and real-image evaluations.

M1.justification: The core paired-image VQA framework, three contrast types, four paradigms and SSCM trait inventory remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and additional validation experiments do not establish a redesign of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 extends image evaluation beyond FLUX-generated imagery to Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image generations and real PATA photographs. The PATA evaluation covers cooking and programming across five racial/ethnic groups and two genders, with matched synthetic counterparts. The original identity inventory and 75 activities remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figures 13–14 expand the evaluated model comparisons beyond LLaVA-1.6, Llama-3.2 and DeepSeek-VL2 to GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3-Pro Preview and Qwen3-VL-30B. These figures establish participation of seven models despite some appendix prose describing only five.

E3.justification: New protocols include balanced 100-pair cooking evaluations, matched real/synthetic comparisons with error summaries, paraphrased and positional response options, and a 1,200-pair human validation study. Existing decoding settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 describes both/none options for identity questions that Section 4.2 still specifies as binary, leaving that detail unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of prompt paraphrases, identity versus left/right responses, image-generator dependence, and real/synthetic agreement. It also adds paired-identity distinguishability validation and multiple LLaVA attention case studies. These substantially extend v1's supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 9–10 introduce annotator agreement percentages and Cohen's kappa for image quality and identity distinguishability; v1 offered qualitative image-quality assurance. Fisher's exact tests and z-score reporting remain, with no newly documented seeds, repeated-run counts or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model, generator, real-image, annotation and robustness results. Examples include 59–70% full paraphrase matches in Table 11 and a reported 2.9347 percentage-point real/synthetic mean absolute difference in Table 12. Main-figure results remain, while v1's standalone DeepSeek factuality/decision breakdowns in Figures 8–15 are omitted.

T1.justification: Section 5 corrects the mathematical interpretation of negative PairComp: v1 says identity i2 is selected more, while v2 correctly describes reduced selection of i1 relative to its without-i2 baseline. The formula itself is unchanged; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: 30M+ paired images, 75 activities, eight identity dimensions, four socially grounded evaluation paradigms, and context-dependent, sometimes conflicting biases. The appendix additions primarily support and qualify these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of generator-induced confounding, identity-label versus spatial-reasoning confounds, context-dependent interpretations of bias magnitude, and non-causal relationships between paradigms. It also interprets the new cross-generator and real-image findings and expands the applicability limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds annotator instructions and demographics, visual-cue criteria, explicit gendered prompt examples, exact paraphrases and proprietary API expenditure. Existing hardware, decoding parameters and code/data access are retained. The earlier exact 50-image interpretability sample is replaced by an unspecified small sample.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 and new Table 2 expand comparisons with existing benchmarks, particularly Girrbach et al.'s real-image gender-bias work. Additional citations support cultural visual cues, real-image evaluation and spatial reasoning, while the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain intact. Local edits clarify terminology and task descriptions, repair cross-references and expand dataset explanations. An appendix roadmap is added, computation details move into A.3, and retained additional results move into A.10.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison and validation tables, paired-image examples, multi-model heatmaps, real-image and response-format plots, and a multi-case attention figure. It removes the old DeepSeek panels, recolors retained polarity heatmaps and moves the activity-taxonomy table into the main text. Main Figures 1–7 remain identical.

improvement.justification: The added generator, real-image, prompt and response-format checks make the benchmark more assessable than v1's largely qualitative validation. Explicit confounding and non-causality discussions also improve interpretation. However, the extensions are narrow, Table 9 contains annotation counts inconsistent with the stated sample size, and A.5 overstates consistency relative to Figure 14. These issues limit the net improvement despite the substantial expansion.
